name: Carbamazepine

fields.mechanism_of_action: Tegretol has demonstrated anticonvulsant properties in rats and mice with electrically and chemically induced seizures. It appears to act by reducing polysynaptic responses and blocking the post-tetanic potentiation. Tegretol greatly reduces or abolishes pain induced by stimulation of the infraorbital nerve in cats and rats. It depresses thalamic potential and bulbar and polysynaptic reflexes, including the linguomandibular reflex in cats. Tegretol is chemically unrelated to other anticonvulsants or other drugs used to control the pain of trigeminal neuralgia. The mechanism of action remains unknown (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Mechanism of Action). The principal metabolite of Tegretol, carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide, has anticonvulsant activity as demonstrated in several in vivo animal models of seizures; though clinical activity for the epoxide has been postulated, the significance of its activity with respect to the safety and efficacy of Tegretol has not been established (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Mechanism of Action). The UK SmPC adds: carbamazepine stabilises hyperexcited nerve membranes, inhibits repetitive neuronal discharges, and reduces synaptic propagation of excitatory impulses; prevention of repetitive firing of sodium-dependent action potentials in depolarised neurons via use- and voltage-dependent blockade of sodium channels may be its main mechanism of action. Whereas reduction of glutamate release and stabilisation of neuronal membranes may account for the antiepileptic effects, the depressant effect on dopamine and noradrenaline turnover could be responsible for the antimanic properties of carbamazepine (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 5.1).
indications: Epilepsy: Tegretol is indicated for use as an anticonvulsant drug. Evidence supporting efficacy as an anticonvulsant was derived from active drug-controlled studies that enrolled patients with the following seizure types: partial seizures with complex symptomatology (psychomotor, temporal lobe) - patients with these seizures appear to show greater improvement than those with other types; generalized tonic-clonic seizures (grand mal); mixed seizure patterns which include the above, or other partial or generalized seizures. Absence seizures (petit mal) do not appear to be controlled by Tegretol (Tegretol US PI, INDICATIONS AND USAGE - Epilepsy). Controlled clinical trials also showed Tegretol effective in the treatment of psychomotor and grand mal seizures (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY).

Trigeminal neuralgia: Tegretol is indicated in the treatment of the pain associated with true trigeminal neuralgia. Beneficial results have also been reported in glossopharyngeal neuralgia. This drug is not a simple analgesic and should not be used for the relief of trivial aches or pains (Tegretol US PI, INDICATIONS AND USAGE - Trigeminal Neuralgia).

UK SmPC only (not an FDA-approved US indication): the paroxysmal pain of trigeminal neuralgia; epilepsy - generalised tonic-clonic and partial seizures, noting Tegretol is not usually effective in absences (petit mal) and myoclonic seizures, and anecdotal evidence suggests seizure exacerbation may occur in patients with atypical absences; for the prophylaxis of manic-depressive psychosis in patients unresponsive to lithium therapy (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.1).

Bipolar disorder scope note: the US FDA Tegretol Prescribing Information does NOT list bipolar disorder or any psychiatric indication; in the US, carbamazepine is not FDA-approved for bipolar disorder. The bipolar (prophylaxis of manic-depressive psychosis unresponsive to lithium) indication is licensed in the UK per the Tegretol UK SmPC, section 4.1.
contraindications: Tegretol should not be used in patients with a history of previous bone marrow depression, hypersensitivity to the drug, or known sensitivity to any of the tricyclic compounds, such as amitriptyline, desipramine, imipramine, protriptyline, nortriptyline, etc. (Tegretol US PI, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

On theoretical grounds, use with monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors is not recommended. Before administration of Tegretol, MAO inhibitors should be discontinued for a minimum of 14 days, or longer if the clinical situation permits (Tegretol US PI, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Coadministration of carbamazepine and nefazodone may result in insufficient plasma concentrations of nefazodone and its active metabolite to achieve a therapeutic effect. Coadministration of carbamazepine with nefazodone is contraindicated (Tegretol US PI, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
Tegretol should not be used in patients positive for HLA-B*1502 unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk (Tegretol US PI, BOXED WARNING and WARNINGS - SJS/TEN and HLA-B*1502 Allele).

UK SmPC additional contraindications: known hypersensitivity to carbamazepine or structurally related drugs (e.g. tricyclic antidepressants) or any other component of the formulation; patients with atrioventricular block; a history of bone marrow depression or a history of hepatic porphyrias (e.g. acute intermittent porphyria, variegate porphyria, porphyria cutanea tarda); the use of Tegretol is contraindicated in combination with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) - before administering Tegretol, MAOIs should be discontinued for a minimum of 2 weeks, or longer if the clinical situation permits (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, sections 4.3 and 4.5).
side_effects: Most frequently observed adverse reactions, particularly during initial phases of therapy: dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness, nausea, and vomiting. To minimize the possibility of such reactions, therapy should be initiated at the lowest dosage recommended (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Hemopoietic system: aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, bone marrow depression, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, leukocytosis, eosinophilia, acute intermittent porphyria, variegate porphyria, porphyria cutanea tarda (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Skin: TEN and SJS (see BOXED WARNING), Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis (AGEP), pruritic and erythematous rashes, urticaria, photosensitivity reactions, fixed drug eruption, generalized bullous fixed drug eruption, alterations in skin pigmentation, exfoliative dermatitis, erythema multiforme and nodosum, purpura, aggravation of disseminated lupus erythematosus, alopecia, diaphoresis, onychomadesis and hirsutism. In certain cases, discontinuation of therapy may be necessary (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Cardiovascular system: congestive heart failure, edema, aggravation of hypertension, hypotension, syncope and collapse, aggravation of coronary artery disease, arrhythmias and AV block, thrombophlebitis, thromboembolism (e.g., pulmonary embolism), and adenopathy or lymphadenopathy. Some of these cardiovascular complications have resulted in fatalities. Myocardial infarction has been associated with other tricyclic compounds (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Liver: abnormalities in liver function tests, cholestatic and hepatocellular jaundice, hepatitis, very rare cases of hepatic failure; rare instances of vanishing bile duct syndrome have been reported (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS and PRECAUTIONS - General).
Pancreatic: pancreatitis (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Respiratory system: pulmonary hypersensitivity characterized by fever, dyspnea, pneumonitis, or pneumonia (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Genitourinary system: urinary frequency, acute urinary retention, oliguria with elevated blood pressure, azotemia, renal failure, and impotence; albuminuria, glycosuria, elevated BUN, and microscopic deposits in the urine have also been reported; rare reports of impaired male fertility and/or abnormal spermatogenesis (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Nervous system: dizziness, drowsiness, disturbances of coordination, confusion, headache, fatigue, blurred vision, visual hallucinations, transient diplopia, oculomotor disturbances, nystagmus, speech disturbances, abnormal involuntary movements, peripheral neuritis and paresthesias, depression with agitation, talkativeness, tinnitus, hyperacusis, neuroleptic malignant syndrome; isolated cases of neuroleptic malignant syndrome have been reported both with and without concomitant use of psychotropic drugs (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Digestive system: nausea, vomiting, gastric distress and abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, anorexia, and dryness of the mouth and pharynx, including glossitis and stomatitis (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Eyes: scattered punctate cortical lens opacities, increased intraocular pressure, as well as conjunctivitis (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Musculoskeletal system: aching joints and muscles, and leg cramps (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Metabolism/endocrine: fever and chills; hyponatremia (dose-related, often SIADH; elderly and patients on diuretics at greater risk); decreased levels of plasma calcium; osteoporosis; thyroid function tests may show decreased values; interference with some pregnancy tests has been reported; altered lipids (elevated cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides) occasionally reported (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General, ADVERSE REACTIONS and PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests).

UK SmPC frequency-ranked highlights (CIOMS III): very common - leucopenia, ataxia, dizziness, somnolence, vomiting, nausea, urticaria, fatigue, gamma-glutamyltransferase increased; common - thrombocytopenia, eosinophilia, diplopia, headache, accommodation disorders, dry mouth, oedema/fluid retention/weight increase/hyponatraemia/decreased blood osmolarity (ADH-like effect), blood alkaline phosphatase increased; uncommon - abnormal involuntary movements, nystagmus, diarrhoea, constipation, dermatitis allergic/exfoliative (rare); rare - leucocytosis, lymphadenopathy, delayed multi-organ hypersensitivity, cardiac conduction disorders, folate deficiency, hallucinations, depression, hepatitis, vanishing bile duct syndrome; very rare - agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia, pancytopenia, anaphylactic reaction, angioedema, DRESS, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, aseptic meningitis, hepatic failure, SJS/TEN, congestive cardiac failure, circulatory collapse, pulmonary hypersensitivity, pancreatitis; not known - bone marrow depression, HHV-6 reactivation, hyperammonaemia, sedation, memory impairment, falls, hypogammaglobulinaemia (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.8).

There have been reports of decreased bone mineral density, osteopenia, osteoporosis and fractures in patients on long-term therapy; a case of aseptic meningitis with myoclonus and peripheral eosinophilia has been reported with rechallenge positivity (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.8).

dosage.adult: Epilepsy, adults and children over 12 years of age (US label): initial either 200 mg twice a day for tablets and XR tablets, or 1 teaspoon four times a day for suspension (400 mg/day). Increase at weekly intervals by adding up to 200 mg/day using a twice a day regimen of Tegretol-XR or a three times a day or four times a day regimen of the other formulations until optimal response is obtained. Dosage generally should not exceed 1000 mg daily in children 12 to 15 years of age, and 1200 mg daily in patients above 15 years of age; doses up to 1600 mg daily have been used in adults in rare instances. Maintenance: adjust dosage to the minimum effective level, usually 800 to 1200 mg daily (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Epilepsy). Trigeminal neuralgia (US label): initial on the first day either 100 mg twice a day for tablets or XR tablets, or 1/2 teaspoon four times a day for suspension, for a total daily dose of 200 mg; increase by up to 200 mg/day using increments of 100 mg every 12 hours for tablets or XR tablets, or 50 mg (1/2 teaspoon) four times a day for suspension, only as needed to achieve freedom from pain; do not exceed 1200 mg daily. Maintenance: control of pain can be maintained in most patients with 400 to 800 mg daily; some patients may be maintained on as little as 200 mg daily, while others may require as much as 1200 mg daily. At least once every 3 months throughout the treatment period, attempts should be made to reduce the dose to the minimum effective level or even to discontinue the drug (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Trigeminal Neuralgia). UK SmPC adult epilepsy: gradually increasing dosage scheme, initially 100-200 mg once or twice daily, slowly increased until the best response is obtained, often 800-1200 mg daily; in some instances 1600 mg or even 2000 mg daily may be necessary (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2). UK SmPC trigeminal neuralgia: slowly raise initial dosage of 200-400 mg daily until freedom from pain is achieved (normally at 200 mg 3-4 times daily); in the majority of patients 200 mg 3 or 4 times a day is sufficient to maintain a pain-free state; some instances may need 1600 mg daily; once in remission, gradually reduce to the lowest maintenance level; in elderly patients an initial dose of 100 mg twice daily is recommended (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2). UK SmPC bipolar prophylaxis (patients unresponsive to lithium): initial starting dose of 400 mg daily in divided doses, increasing gradually until symptoms are controlled or a total of 1600 mg given in divided doses is reached; the usual dosage range is 400-600 mg daily in divided doses (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2). Medication should be taken with meals (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Tegretol may be used alone or with other anticonvulsants; when added to existing anticonvulsant therapy, add gradually while the other anticonvulsants are maintained or gradually decreased, except phenytoin, which may have to be increased (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Epilepsy, Combination Therapy). Suspension produces higher peak levels than the same tablet dose; start with low doses and increase slowly (children 6 to 12 years: 1/2 teaspoon four times a day); when converting from tablets to suspension, give the same number of mg per day in smaller, more frequent doses (twice a day tablets to three times a day suspension); when converting from conventional tablets to Tegretol-XR, administer the same total daily mg dose (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
dosage.maximum: Epilepsy: generally should not exceed 1000 mg daily in children 12-15 years of age, and 1200 mg daily in patients above 15 years of age; doses up to 1600 mg daily have been used in adults in rare instances (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Epilepsy). Children 6-12 years: generally should not exceed 1000 mg daily (US label) / 1000 mg/day (UK SmPC 6-15 years) (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Epilepsy; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2 - Maximum recommended dose). Children under 6 years: no recommendation can be made regarding safety above 35 mg/kg/24 hours; ordinarily optimal response is achieved below 35 mg/kg/day (35 mg/kg/24 hr, US and UK) (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Epilepsy; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2). Trigeminal neuralgia: do not exceed 1200 mg daily; up to 1600 mg daily may be needed in some instances per UK SmPC, but the US label states not to exceed 1200 mg daily (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Trigeminal Neuralgia; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2). Bipolar prophylaxis (UK): up to 1600 mg given in divided doses; usual range 400-600 mg daily (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2). Usual adult therapeutic plasma levels are 4 to 12 mcg/mL (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Pharmacokinetics).

interactions: Agents that increase carbamazepine (CYP3A4 inhibitors inhibit Tegretol metabolism): aprepitant, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, danazol, diltiazem, macrolides (e.g., erythromycin, clarithromycin), fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, trazodone, omeprazole, oxybutynin, isoniazid, niacinamide (nicotinamide), azoles (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, fluconazole, voriconazole), acetazolamide, verapamil, ticlopidine, grapefruit juice, and protease inhibitors. Close monitoring of carbamazepine levels is indicated and dosage adjustment may be required (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions, Agents That May Affect Tegretol Plasma Levels). UK SmPC also lists paroxetine, vigabatrin, dextropropoxyphene, olanzapine, ritonavir, and possibly cimetidine/omeprazole; alternative anticonvulsants may be recommended in patients treated with voriconazole or itraconazole (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Human microsomal epoxide hydrolase inhibitors increase carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide plasma concentrations: adjust Tegretol dosage and/or monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly with loxapine, quetiapine, valproic acid, or brivaracetam (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions). UK SmPC adds progabide, valnoctamide, valpromide, primidone (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Agents that decrease carbamazepine levels (CYP3A4 inducers): cisplatin, doxorubicin HCl, felbamate, fosphenytoin, rifampin, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, methsuximide, theophylline, aminophylline (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions). UK SmPC adds oxcarbazepine, clonazepam (possibly), isotretinoin, St John's wort (Hypericum perforatum); recommends adjusting the plasma concentration of phenytoin to 13 micrograms/mL before adding carbamazepine to avoid phenytoin intoxication and subtherapeutic carbamazepine (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Tegretol is a potent inducer of hepatic CYP3A4 and also induces CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8/9/19; it reduces plasma concentrations of co-medications mainly metabolized by these enzymes. Monitor concentrations or adjust dosage when used with such agents (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions, Effect of Tegretol on Plasma Levels of Concomitant Agents).

Aripiprazole: when carbamazepine is added to aripiprazole, the aripiprazole dose should be doubled; additional increases based on clinical evaluation; if carbamazepine is later withdrawn, reduce the aripiprazole dose (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).
Tacrolimus: when carbamazepine is used with tacrolimus, monitor tacrolimus blood concentrations and adjust dosage appropriately (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).

Temsirolimus: avoid concomitant strong CYP3A4 inducers such as carbamazepine; if coadministration is necessary, consider adjusting temsirolimus dosage (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).

Lapatinib: concomitant use should generally be avoided; if carbamazepine is started in a patient already taking lapatinib, gradually titrate the lapatinib dose up; if carbamazepine is discontinued, reduce the lapatinib dose (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).

Nefazodone: concomitant use results in plasma concentrations of nefazodone and its active metabolite insufficient to achieve a therapeutic effect; coadministration of carbamazepine with nefazodone is contraindicated (Tegretol US PI, CONTRAINDICATIONS and PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).

Valproate/valproic acid: monitor concentrations of valproate when Tegretol is introduced or withdrawn in patients using valproic acid (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions). Carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide levels may be raised by valproic acid (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).

Decreased levels of concomitant medications (monitor concentrations or adjust dosage): acetaminophen, albendazole, alprazolam, aprepitant, buprenorphine, bupropion, citalopram, clonazepam, clozapine, corticosteroids (e.g., prednisolone, dexamethasone), cyclosporine, dicumarol, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (e.g., felodipine), doxycycline, eslicarbazepine, ethosuximide, everolimus, haloperidol, imatinib, itraconazole, lamotrigine, levothyroxine, methadone, methsuximide, mianserin, midazolam, olanzapine, oral and other hormonal contraceptives, oxcarbazepine, paliperidone, phensuximide, phenytoin, praziquantel, protease inhibitors, risperidone, sertraline, sirolimus, tadalafil, theophylline, tiagabine, topiramate, tramadol, trazodone, tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., imipramine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline), valproate, warfarin, ziprasidone, zonisamide (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions). UK SmPC additionally lists clobazam, digoxin, simvastatin, atorvastatin, lovastatin, ivabradine, buprenorphine, paracetamol (long-term coadministration associated with hepatotoxicity), hormonal contraceptives and products containing oestrogens/progesterones, rifabutin, and mephenytoin (rare increased levels) (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Cyclophosphamide: an inactive prodrug converted to its active metabolite partly by CYP3A; the rate of metabolism and leukopenic activity are reportedly increased by chronic coadministration of CYP3A4 inducers; potential for increased cyclophosphamide toxicity when coadministered with carbamazepine (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions, Other Drug Interactions).

Lithium: concomitant administration of carbamazepine and lithium may increase the risk of neurotoxic side effects; neurotoxicity may occur in spite of lithium plasma concentrations being within the therapeutic range (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).
Olanzapine, dantrolene, or ibuprofen: concomitant use may increase plasma carbamazepine levels (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).
Isoniazid: concomitant use has been reported to increase isoniazid-induced hepatotoxicity (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Hormonal contraceptives: concomitant use with hormonal contraceptive products (e.g., oral, and levonorgestrel subdermal implant contraceptives) may render the contraceptives less effective because plasma concentrations of the hormones may be decreased; breakthrough bleeding and unintended pregnancies have been reported; alternative or back-up methods of contraception should be considered (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions). UK SmPC: women of childbearing potential should use highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least two weeks after stopping; at least one effective method (e.g., intra-uterine device) or two complementary forms including a barrier method; patients requiring hormonal contraception should receive a preparation containing not less than 50 micrograms oestrogen or use an alternative non-hormonal method (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, sections 4.4, 4.5 and 4.6).

Non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agents (pancuronium, vecuronium, rocuronium, cisatracurium): resistance to their neuromuscular blocking action has occurred in patients chronically administered carbamazepine; monitor closely for more rapid recovery from neuromuscular blockade than expected; infusion rate requirements may be higher; carbamazepine may antagonise these agents and their dosage should be raised (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Direct-acting oral anticoagulants (rivaroxaban, apixaban, dabigatran, and edoxaban): concomitant use is expected to result in decreased plasma concentrations that may be insufficient for the intended therapeutic effect; in general, coadministration should be avoided (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions). UK SmPC: if concomitant use is necessary, closer monitoring of signs and symptoms of thrombosis is recommended (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5). Warfarin and other oral anticoagulants: decreased levels, monitoring or dosage adjustment may be necessary (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).

Tegretol suspension must not be administered simultaneously with other liquid medicinal agents or diluents: mixing with chlorpromazine solution (both generic and brand name, Thorazine) or liquid thioridazine (Mellaril) results in an orange rubbery precipitate; a patient passed an orange rubbery precipitate in his stool after ingesting Tegretol suspension immediately followed by Thorazine solution (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

Monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors: before administration of Tegretol, MAO inhibitors should be discontinued for a minimum of 14 days, or longer if the clinical situation permits (US label); UK SmPC contraindicates the combination and specifies a minimum of 2 weeks (Tegretol US PI, CONTRAINDICATIONS; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, sections 4.3 and 4.5).
Levetiracetam: concomitant use has been reported to increase carbamazepine-induced toxicity (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).
Metoclopramide or major tranquillisers (e.g., haloperidol, thioridazine): combined use may result in an increase in neurological side-effects (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).
Diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide, furosemide): concomitant medication with Tegretol may lead to symptomatic hyponatraemia (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).
Alterations of thyroid function have been reported in combination therapy with other anticonvulsant medications (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).
Methotrexate is not addressed in the Tegretol labels; no statement available - not included as an interaction.
fields.monitoring: Before initiating therapy, a detailed history and physical examination should be made (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General). For genetically at-risk patients, high-resolution HLA-B*1502 typing is recommended; the test is positive if either one or two HLA-B*1502 alleles are detected and negative if none are detected (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests; UK SmPC recommends screening patients of Han Chinese and Thai origin before starting, section 4.2). Complete pretreatment blood counts, including platelets and possibly reticulocytes and serum iron, should be obtained as a baseline; if a patient in the course of treatment exhibits low or decreased white blood cell or platelet counts, the patient should be monitored closely, and discontinuation of the drug should be considered if any evidence of significant bone marrow depression develops (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests and BOXED WARNING). UK SmPC: monitor periodically thereafter; discontinue if leucopenia is severe, progressive or accompanied by clinical manifestations such as fever or sore throat, or if any evidence of significant bone marrow depression appears (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4). Baseline and periodic evaluations of liver function, particularly in patients with a history of liver disease, must be performed during treatment; carbamazepine should be discontinued, based on clinical judgment, if indicated by newly occurring or worsening clinical or laboratory evidence of liver dysfunction or hepatic damage, or in the case of active liver disease (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests). Baseline and periodic eye examinations, including slit-lamp, funduscopy, and tonometry, are recommended since many phenothiazines and related drugs have been shown to cause eye changes (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests). Baseline and periodic complete urinalysis and BUN determinations are recommended for patients treated with this agent because of observed renal dysfunction (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests; UK SmPC, section 4.4). Monitoring of blood levels has increased the efficacy and safety of anticonvulsants; this monitoring may be particularly useful in cases of dramatic increase in seizure frequency and for verification of compliance; measurement of drug serum levels may aid in determining the cause of toxicity when more than one medication is being used; usual therapeutic range 4-12 mcg/mL (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests and CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY). UK SmPC lists specific scenarios where plasma-level monitoring is useful: dramatic increase in seizure frequency/verification of compliance; during pregnancy; when treating children or adolescents; suspected absorption disorders; suspected toxicity when more than one drug is used (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4). Thyroid function tests have been reported to show decreased values with Tegretol administered alone; thyroid function monitoring is suggested to adjust the dosage of thyroid replacement therapy in patients with hypothyroidism (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4). Interference with some pregnancy tests has been reported (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests). Monitor for signs of suicidal ideation and behaviour in all patients treated with AEDs for any indication, as early as one week after starting, and persisting for the duration of treatment assessed (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Suicidal Behavior and Ideation). Serum sodium levels should be measured prior to initiating carbamazepine therapy in patients with pre-existing renal conditions associated with low sodium or in patients treated concomitantly with sodium-lowering medicinal products (e.g., diuretics), then after approximately two weeks and at monthly intervals for the first three months during therapy, or according to clinical need; the risk factors may apply especially to elderly patients (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Hyponatremia). Monitor patients for falls risk recurrently in long-term treatment (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Falls). Monitor patients on Tegretol suspension for signs of propylene glycol toxicity, including hemolysis, hyperosmolarity with anion gap metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, and CNS toxicity; patients less than 5 years of age, particularly neonates, are at highest risk (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Propylene Glycol Toxicity). Surveillance after overdose: respiration, cardiac function (ECG monitoring), blood pressure, body temperature, pupillary reflexes, and kidney and bladder function should be monitored for several days (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Treatment, Surveillance).
fields.patient_counselling: Patients should be informed of the availability of a Medication Guide, and they should be instructed to read the Medication Guide before taking Tegretol (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Patients should be made aware of the early toxic signs and symptoms of a potential hematologic problem, as well as dermatologic, hypersensitivity or hepatic reactions. These symptoms may include, but are not limited to, fever, sore throat, rash, ulcers in the mouth, easy bruising, lymphadenopathy and petechial or purpuric hemorrhage, and in the case of liver reactions, anorexia, nausea/vomiting, or jaundice. The patient should be advised that, because these signs and symptoms may signal a serious reaction, they must report any occurrence immediately to a physician, even if mild or when occurring after extended use (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Patients should be advised that serious skin reactions have been reported in association with Tegretol; in the event a skin reaction should occur, patients should consult their physician immediately (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). The Medication Guide warns that TEGRETOL may cause rare but serious skin rashes that can lead to death, more likely within the first four months of treatment, and that people of Asian descent may need a genetic blood test before taking TEGRETOL; do not stop taking TEGRETOL without first talking to a healthcare provider, as stopping suddenly can cause serious problems (Tegretol US PI, MEDICATION GUIDE). Patients should be advised that anaphylactic reactions and angioedema (swelling of the face, eyes, lips, or tongue, or difficulty in swallowing or breathing) may occur; advise patients to immediately report such signs and symptoms and to stop taking the drug until they have consulted with their healthcare provider (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Patients, their caregivers, and families should be counseled that AEDs, including Tegretol, may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior and should be advised of the need to be alert for the emergence or worsening of symptoms of depression, any unusual changes in mood or behavior, or the emergence of suicidal thoughts, behavior, or thoughts about self-harm; behaviors of concern should be reported immediately to healthcare providers (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Patients should be advised to report to their doctors the use of any other prescription or non-prescription medications or herbal products, because Tegretol may interact with some drugs (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Caution should be exercised if alcohol is taken in combination with Tegretol therapy, due to a possible additive sedative effect (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Since dizziness and drowsiness may occur, patients should be cautioned about the hazards of operating machinery or automobiles or engaging in other potentially dangerous tasks (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). Patients should be encouraged to enroll in the NAAED Pregnancy Registry if they become pregnant; to enroll, call the toll-free number 1-888-233-2334 (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients and WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy). Women of childbearing potential should be informed that carbamazepine may cause fetal harm, should use highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least two weeks after stopping (hormonal contraceptives may be ineffective due to enzyme induction), and should consult their physician as soon as they plan a pregnancy or if they become pregnant (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, sections 4.4 and 4.6). Pregnant patients or those becoming pregnant should notify their healthcare provider about pregnancy registry enrollment; the Medication Guide provides the registry number 1-888-233-2334 (Tegretol US PI, MEDICATION GUIDE). Shake the suspension well before using; Tegretol-XR tablets must be swallowed whole and never crushed or chewed, should be inspected for chips or cracks, and damaged tablets or tablets without a release portal should not be consumed; the XR tablet coating is not absorbed and is excreted in the feces, where it may be noticeable in the stool (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, HOW SUPPLIED and MEDICATION GUIDE). Medication should be taken with meals (Tegretol US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Like other antiepileptic drugs, TEGRETOL may cause suicidal thoughts or actions in a very small number of people, about 1 in 500 (Tegretol US PI, MEDICATION GUIDE). Patients may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 (Tegretol US PI, MEDICATION GUIDE).
warnings: BOXED WARNING: SERIOUS DERMATOLOGIC REACTIONS AND HLA-B*1502 ALLELE - SERIOUS AND SOMETIMES FATAL DERMATOLOGIC REACTIONS, INCLUDING TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS (TEN) AND STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME (SJS), HAVE BEEN REPORTED DURING TREATMENT WITH TEGRETOL. THESE REACTIONS ARE ESTIMATED TO OCCUR IN 1 TO 6 PER 10,000 NEW USERS IN COUNTRIES WITH MAINLY CAUCASIAN POPULATIONS, BUT THE RISK IN SOME ASIAN COUNTRIES IS ESTIMATED TO BE ABOUT 10 TIMES HIGHER. STUDIES IN PATIENTS OF CHINESE ANCESTRY HAVE FOUND A STRONG ASSOCIATION BETWEEN THE RISK OF DEVELOPING SJS/TEN AND THE PRESENCE OF HLA-B*1502, AN INHERITED ALLELIC VARIANT OF THE HLA-B GENE. HLA-B*1502 IS FOUND ALMOST EXCLUSIVELY IN PATIENTS WITH ANCESTRY ACROSS BROAD AREAS OF ASIA. PATIENTS WITH ANCESTRY IN GENETICALLY AT-RISK POPULATIONS SHOULD BE SCREENED FOR THE PRESENCE OF HLA-B*1502 PRIOR TO INITIATING TREATMENT WITH TEGRETOL. PATIENTS TESTING POSITIVE FOR THE ALLELE SHOULD NOT BE TREATED WITH TEGRETOL UNLESS THE BENEFIT CLEARLY OUTWEIGHS THE RISK (SEE WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, LABORATORY TESTS). (Tegretol US PI, Boxed Warning)

BOXED WARNING: APLASTIC ANEMIA AND AGRANULOCYTOSIS - APLASTIC ANEMIA AND AGRANULOCYTOSIS HAVE BEEN REPORTED IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE USE OF TEGRETOL. DATA FROM A POPULATION-BASED CASE CONTROL STUDY DEMONSTRATE THAT THE RISK OF DEVELOPING THESE REACTIONS IS 5 TO 8 TIMES GREATER THAN IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. HOWEVER, THE OVERALL RISK OF THESE REACTIONS IN THE UNTREATED GENERAL POPULATION IS LOW, APPROXIMATELY SIX PATIENTS PER ONE MILLION POPULATION PER YEAR FOR AGRANULOCYTOSIS AND TWO PATIENTS PER ONE MILLION POPULATION PER YEAR FOR APLASTIC ANEMIA. ALTHOUGH REPORTS OF TRANSIENT OR PERSISTENT DECREASED PLATELET OR WHITE BLOOD CELL COUNTS ARE NOT UNCOMMON IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE USE OF TEGRETOL, DATA ARE NOT AVAILABLE TO ESTIMATE ACCURATELY THEIR INCIDENCE OR OUTCOME. HOWEVER, THE VAST MAJORITY OF THE CASES OF LEUKOPENIA HAVE NOT PROGRESSED TO THE MORE SERIOUS CONDITIONS OF APLASTIC ANEMIA OR AGRANULOCYTOSIS. BECAUSE OF THE VERY LOW INCIDENCE OF AGRANULOCYTOSIS AND APLASTIC ANEMIA, THE VAST MAJORITY OF MINOR HEMATOLOGIC CHANGES OBSERVED IN MONITORING OF PATIENTS ON TEGRETOL ARE UNLIKELY TO SIGNAL THE OCCURRENCE OF EITHER ABNORMALITY. NONETHELESS, COMPLETE PRETREATMENT HEMATOLOGICAL TESTING SHOULD BE OBTAINED AS A BASELINE. IF A PATIENT IN THE COURSE OF TREATMENT EXHIBITS LOW OR DECREASED WHITE BLOOD CELL OR PLATELET COUNTS, THE PATIENT SHOULD BE MONITORED CLOSELY. DISCONTINUATION OF THE DRUG SHOULD BE CONSIDERED IF ANY EVIDENCE OF SIGNIFICANT BONE MARROW DEPRESSION DEVELOPS. (Tegretol US PI, Boxed Warning)

Before prescribing Tegretol, the physician should be thoroughly familiar with the details of this prescribing information, particularly regarding use with other drugs, especially those which accentuate toxicity potential (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS).

Serious dermatologic reactions: serious and sometimes fatal dermatologic reactions, including TEN and SJS, have been reported with Tegretol treatment; risk about 1 to 6 per 10,000 new users in mainly Caucasian countries, about 10 times higher in some Asian countries. Fixed drug eruption (FDE) has been reported, and with repeated exposure may progress to generalized bullous fixed drug eruption (GBFDE), a serious skin reaction which may resemble SJS/TEN. Tegretol should be discontinued at the first sign of a rash, unless the rash is clearly not drug related; if signs or symptoms suggest SJS/TEN, FDE, or GBFDE, use of this drug should not be resumed, and alternative therapy should be considered (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Serious Dermatologic Reactions).

SJS/TEN and HLA-B*1502 allele: retrospective case-control studies found a strong association in patients of Chinese ancestry between SJS/TEN risk and HLA-B*1502. Notable variation across Asian populations: greater than 15% positive in Hong Kong, Thailand, Malaysia, and parts of the Philippines, about 10% in Taiwan and 4% in North China; South Asians including Indians average 2% to 4% (higher in some groups); HLA-B*1502 is present in less than 1% in Japan and Korea and is largely absent in individuals not of Asian origin (e.g., Caucasians, African-Americans, Hispanics, Native Americans). Prior to initiating Tegretol therapy, testing for HLA-B*1502 should be performed in patients with ancestry in populations in which HLA-B*1502 may be present; Tegretol should not be used in patients positive for the allele unless the benefits clearly outweigh the risks. Tested patients found negative are thought to have a low risk of SJS/TEN. Over 90% of Tegretol-treated patients who will experience SJS/TEN have this reaction within the first few months of treatment (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - SJS/TEN and HLA-B*1502 Allele).

Hypersensitivity reactions and HLA-A*3101 allele: retrospective case-control studies in patients of European, Korean, and Japanese ancestry found a moderate association between risk of hypersensitivity reactions (including SJS/TEN, maculopapular eruptions, and DRESS) and HLA-A*3101. HLA-A*3101 is expected to be carried by more than 15% of Japanese, Native American, Southern Indian (e.g., Tamil Nadu), and some Arabic ancestry; up to about 10% in Han Chinese, Korean, European, Latin American, and other Indian ancestry; and up to about 5% in African-Americans and patients of Thai, Taiwanese, and Chinese (Hong Kong) ancestry. The risks and benefits of Tegretol therapy should be weighed before considering Tegretol in patients known to be positive for HLA-A*3101 (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Hypersensitivity Reactions and HLA-A*3101 Allele).

The HLA-B*1502 allele has not been found to predict risk of less severe adverse cutaneous reactions (e.g., maculopapular eruption) or to predict DRESS (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - SJS/TEN and HLA-B*1502 Allele).

DRESS/multiorgan hypersensitivity: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms has occurred with Tegretol; some events have been fatal or life-threatening. DRESS typically presents with fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, and/or facial swelling, in association with other organ system involvement such as hepatitis, nephritis, hematologic abnormalities, myocarditis, or myositis, sometimes resembling an acute viral infection; eosinophilia is often present. Early manifestations (e.g., fever, lymphadenopathy) may be present even though rash is not evident; if such signs or symptoms are present, the patient should be evaluated immediately, and Tegretol should be discontinued if an alternative etiology cannot be established (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - DRESS/Multiorgan Hypersensitivity).

Hypersensitivity: reactions to carbamazepine have been reported in patients who previously experienced this reaction to anticonvulsants, including phenytoin, primidone, and phenobarbital; if such history is present, benefits and risks should be carefully considered and, if carbamazepine is initiated, signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity carefully monitored. About a third of patients who have had hypersensitivity reactions to carbamazepine also experience hypersensitivity reactions with oxcarbazepine (Trileptal) (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Hypersensitivity).

Anaphylaxis and angioedema: rare cases of anaphylaxis and angioedema involving the larynx, glottis, lips, and eyelids have been reported after first or subsequent doses; angioedema associated with laryngeal edema can be fatal. If a patient develops such reactions, the drug should be discontinued and an alternative treatment started; these patients should not be rechallenged (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Anaphylaxis and Angioedema).

Propylene glycol toxicity: Tegretol suspension contains propylene glycol (25 mg per mL). Patients less than 5 years of age are at highest risk, and a safe level for propylene glycol exposure with repeated administration has not been established for this age group; neonates (less than 4 weeks of age, full-term or pre-term less than 44 post-menstrual weeks) have immature metabolic and renal clearance. Tegretol suspension should only be used in neonates after careful risk-benefit assessment if no therapeutic alternatives are available. At the maximum epilepsy dose (35 mg/kg/day), exposure to propylene glycol will be 44 mg/kg/day; consider total daily intake from all sources (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Propylene Glycol Toxicity).

Suicidal behavior and ideation: AEDs, including Tegretol, increase the risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior in patients taking these drugs for any indication. Pooled analyses of 199 placebo-controlled trials of 11 different AEDs showed approximately twice the risk (adjusted relative risk 1.8, 95% CI 1.2, 2.7); estimated incidence 0.43% among 27,863 AED-treated patients vs 0.24% among 16,029 placebo-treated patients - approximately one additional case per 530 patients treated; four suicides in drug-treated patients and none in placebo. The increased risk was observed as early as one week after starting and persisted for the duration of treatment assessed. Patients treated with any AED for any indication should be monitored for emergence or worsening of depression, suicidal thoughts or behavior, and/or any unusual changes in mood or behavior (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Suicidal Behavior and Ideation).

Vanishing bile duct syndrome: rare instances of a cholestatic process involving destruction and disappearance of the intrahepatic bile ducts have been reported; the course ranges from fulminant to indolent; some cases overlap with immunoallergenic syndromes such as multiorgan hypersensitivity (DRESS) and serious dermatologic reactions (e.g., associated with SJS, or with fever and eosinophilia). In some cases hepatic effects may progress despite discontinuation (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General).

Hyponatremia: hyponatremia can occur as a result of treatment with Tegretol, in many cases caused by SIADH; the risk appears to be dose-related; elderly patients and patients treated with diuretics are at greater risk. Signs and symptoms include headache, new or increased seizure frequency, difficulty concentrating, memory impairment, confusion, weakness, and unsteadiness, which can lead to falls. Consider discontinuing Tegretol in patients with symptomatic hyponatremia (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General; see also PRECAUTIONS, General).

Usage in pregnancy: carbamazepine can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman; epidemiological data suggest an association with congenital malformations, including spina bifida; reports also associate carbamazepine with developmental disorders and congenital anomalies (craniofacial defects, cardiovascular malformations, anomalies involving various body systems); developmental delays based on neurobehavioral assessments have been reported (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy).

Tegretol has shown mild anticholinergic activity that may be associated with increased intraocular pressure; patients with increased intraocular pressure should be closely observed during therapy (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General).

Because of the relationship of the drug to other tricyclic compounds, the possibility of activation of a latent psychosis and, in elderly patients, of confusion or agitation should be borne in mind (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General).

Avoid Tegretol in patients with a history of hepatic porphyria (e.g., acute intermittent porphyria, variegate porphyria, porphyria cutanea tarda); acute attacks have been reported in such patients receiving Tegretol therapy, and carbamazepine increases porphyrin precursors in rodents (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General).
As with all antiepileptic drugs, Tegretol should be withdrawn gradually to minimize the potential of increased seizure frequency (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General).

Mixed seizure disorder including atypical absence seizures: Tegretol has been associated with increased frequency of generalized convulsions in these patients (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General and INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

Benefit-risk appraisal before prescribing in patients with a history of cardiac conduction disturbance, including second- and third-degree AV heart block; cardiac, hepatic, or renal damage; adverse hematologic or hypersensitivity reaction to other drugs; or interrupted courses of therapy with Tegretol. AV heart block (including second- and third-degree) has been reported following Tegretol treatment, generally but not solely in patients with underlying EKG abnormalities or risk factors for conduction disturbances (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General).

Abrupt discontinuation of any anticonvulsant drug in a responsive epileptic patient may lead to seizures or even status epilepticus with its life-threatening hazards (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

UK SmPC additional warning: serious dermatological reactions (TEN, SJS) are very rare but may require hospitalization as they may be life-threatening and fatal; if signs and symptoms suggestive of severe skin reactions appear, Tegretol should be withdrawn at once and alternative therapy considered; mild transient cutaneous reactions usually disappear within days to weeks, but close surveillance is required because early signs of serious reactions can be difficult to differentiate (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4).

UK SmPC: women of childbearing potential should not use carbamazepine unless the benefit is judged to outweigh the risks following careful consideration of alternative suitable treatment options; before initiation, pregnancy testing should be considered; highly effective contraception is required during treatment and for at least two weeks after stopping; carbamazepine may cause failure of hormonal contraceptives (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Women of childbearing potential).
UK SmPC: increased seizure frequency may occur during switchover from an oral formulation to suppositories (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4).
precautions: Before initiating therapy, a detailed history and physical examination should be made (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General).

Use with caution in patients with a mixed seizure disorder that includes atypical absence seizures, since Tegretol has been associated with increased frequency of generalized convulsions in these patients (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General).

Therapy should be prescribed only after critical benefit-to-risk appraisal in patients with a history of cardiac conduction disturbance, including second- and third-degree AV heart block; cardiac, hepatic, or renal damage; adverse hematologic or hypersensitivity reaction to other drugs, including reactions to other anticonvulsants; or interrupted courses of therapy with Tegretol (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General).

Since a given dose of Tegretol suspension will produce higher peak levels than the same dose given as the tablet, patients given the suspension should be started on lower doses and increased slowly to avoid unwanted side effects (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
Tegretol suspension contains sorbitol and should not be administered to patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - General).

Tegretol suspension should not be administered simultaneously with other liquid medicinal agents or diluents because of precipitate formation with chlorpromazine solution and liquid thioridazine (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

HLA-B*1502 screening: high-resolution typing is recommended for genetically at-risk patients; patients of Han Chinese and Thai origin should whenever possible be screened before starting; tested negative patients have low risk of SJS (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2).

Complete pretreatment blood counts (including platelets and possibly reticulocytes and serum iron) as baseline; monitor closely if low or decreased WBC or platelet counts; discontinue if significant bone marrow depression develops (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests).

Baseline and periodic liver function evaluations, particularly in patients with a history of liver disease, must be performed; discontinue based on clinical judgment if newly occurring or worsening clinical or laboratory evidence of liver dysfunction or hepatic damage, or active liver disease (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests). UK SmPC: GGT elevation is probably due to hepatic enzyme induction and is not, by itself, an indication for withdrawal; severe hepatic reactions occur very rarely and should be urgently evaluated with Tegretol suspended pending the outcome (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4).
Baseline and periodic eye examinations, including slit-lamp, funduscopy, and tonometry, are recommended (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests).

Baseline and periodic complete urinalysis and BUN determinations are recommended because of observed renal dysfunction (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4).

Monitoring of blood levels may be particularly useful in cases of dramatic increase in seizure frequency and for verification of compliance; measurement of drug serum levels may aid in determining the cause of toxicity when more than one medication is being used (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Laboratory Tests).

As with all antiepileptic drugs, Tegretol should be withdrawn gradually; if treatment has to be withdrawn abruptly in a patient with epilepsy, changeover to another anti-epileptic drug should be effected under the cover of a suitable drug (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Dose reduction and withdrawal effects).

Hyponatremia risk: in patients with pre-existing renal conditions associated with low sodium or treated concomitantly with sodium-lowering medicinal products (e.g., diuretics, drugs associated with inappropriate ADH secretion), serum sodium should be measured before starting, after approximately two weeks, then at monthly intervals for the first three months or according to clinical need; risk applies especially to elderly patients; if hyponatraemia is observed, water restriction is an important counter-measure if clinically indicated (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Hyponatremia).

Hypothyroidism: carbamazepine may reduce serum concentrations of thyroid hormones through enzyme induction, requiring an increase in dose of thyroid replacement therapy in patients with hypothyroidism; thyroid function monitoring is suggested (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Hypothyroidism).

Mild anticholinergic activity: patients with increased intraocular pressure and urinary retention should be closely observed during therapy (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Anticholinergic effects; Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General).

Falls: Tegretol treatment has been associated with ataxia, dizziness, somnolence, hypotension, confusional state, sedation, which may lead to falls and fractures or other injuries; complete risk assessment of fall should be considered recurrently for patients on long-term Tegretol treatment, especially those with diseases, conditions, or medications that could exacerbate these effects (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Falls).

Women of childbearing potential: carbamazepine should not be used unless the benefit is judged to outweigh the risks; pregnancy testing should be considered before initiation; use highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least two weeks after stopping; due to enzyme induction, hormonal contraceptives may be ineffective - alternative non-hormonal methods recommended; at least one effective method (e.g., IUD) or two complementary forms including a barrier method; counsel to consult a physician as soon as pregnancy is planned or if pregnancy occurs (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Women of childbearing potential and Endocrinological effects).

Endocrinological: breakthrough bleeding has been reported in women taking Tegretol with hormonal contraceptives; patients taking Tegretol and requiring hormonal contraception should receive a preparation containing not less than 50 micrograms oestrogen or use an alternative non-hormonal method (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Endocrinological effects).

Carcinogenesis: carbamazepine, administered to Sprague-Dawley rats for two years in the diet at doses of 25, 75, and 250 mg/kg/day, resulted in a dose-related increase in hepatocellular tumors in females and benign interstitial cell adenomas in the testes of males; carbamazepine must therefore be considered to be carcinogenic in Sprague-Dawley rats; the significance relative to human use is, at present, unknown (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility).

Impairment of fertility: testicular atrophy occurred in rats receiving Tegretol orally from 4 to 52 weeks at dosage levels of 50 to 400 mg/kg/day; rats in the 2-year diet study had dose-related testicular atrophy and aspermatogenesis; dogs produced a brownish urinary bladder discoloration at 50 mg/kg and higher; relevance to humans unknown (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS). Rare reports of impaired male fertility and/or abnormal spermatogenesis; very rare reports with decreased sperm count and/or motility (US PI ADVERSE REACTIONS; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, sections 4.6 and 4.8).

Cross-hypersensitivity: patients who exhibited hypersensitivity reactions to carbamazepine should be informed that 25-30% may experience hypersensitivity reactions with oxcarbazepine (Trileptal); cross-hypersensitivity can occur between carbamazepine and aromatic antiepileptic drugs (e.g., phenytoin, primidone and phenobarbital) (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Hypersensitivity; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4 - Hypersensitivity).

Abuse and dependence: no evidence of abuse potential has been associated with Tegretol, nor is there evidence of psychological or physical dependence in humans (Tegretol US PI, DRUG ABUSE AND DEPENDENCE).
Tegretol Tablets contain less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per tablet, essentially 'sodium free' (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4).

Different preparations of carbamazepine may vary in bioavailability; to avoid reduced effect or breakthrough seizures or excessive side effects, it may be prudent to avoid changing the formulation (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 5.2 - Absorption).
serious_adverse_reactions: Serious and sometimes fatal dermatologic reactions, including toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) and Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), estimated at 1 to 6 per 10,000 new users in mainly Caucasian populations, about 10 times higher in some Asian countries; most cases appear in the first few months of treatment (Tegretol US PI, BOXED WARNING and WARNINGS - Serious Dermatologic Reactions).

Generalized bullous fixed drug eruption (GBFDE), a serious skin reaction which may resemble SJS/TEN, with repeated exposure in fixed drug eruption (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Serious Dermatologic Reactions).

Aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis: reported; risk 5 to 8 times greater than the general population; overall untreated-population risk approximately six patients per one million per year for agranulocytosis and two per one million per year for aplastic anemia (US); UK baseline estimates 4.7 per million per year for agranulocytosis and 2.0 per million per year for aplastic anaemia (Tegretol US PI, BOXED WARNING; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.4).

Pancytopenia, bone marrow depression; the most severe adverse reactions have been observed in the hemopoietic system and skin, the liver, and the cardiovascular system (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms)/multiorgan hypersensitivity, with some events fatal or life-threatening; may involve hepatitis, nephritis, hematologic abnormalities, myocarditis, or myositis; early manifestations (fever, lymphadenopathy) may be present without rash (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - DRESS/Multiorgan Hypersensitivity).

Anaphylaxis and angioedema involving the larynx, glottis, lips, and eyelids; angioedema associated with laryngeal edema can be fatal; patients should not be rechallenged (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Anaphylaxis and Angioedema).

Hepatic failure (very rare cases), vanishing bile duct syndrome, cholestatic and hepatocellular jaundice, hepatitis; in some cases hepatic effects may progress despite discontinuation (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS and PRECAUTIONS - General).
Pulmonary hypersensitivity characterized by fever, dyspnea, pneumonitis, or pneumonia (very rare) (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Cardiovascular complications with fatalities: congestive heart failure, arrhythmias and AV block, syncope and collapse, thromboembolism (e.g., pulmonary embolism) (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: isolated cases with and without concomitant psychotropic drugs (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Aseptic meningitis accompanied by myoclonus and peripheral eosinophilia; resolved on dechallenge and recurred on rechallenge (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Pancreatitis (rare/very rare) (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.8).

Suicidal behavior or ideation: approximately twice the risk vs placebo (adjusted RR 1.8, 95% CI 1.2, 2.7); about one additional case per 530 patients treated; four suicides in drug-treated patients in the trials (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Suicidal Behavior and Ideation).

Neonatal seizures and/or respiratory depression associated with maternal Tegretol use, and neonatal vomiting, diarrhea, and/or decreased feeding, possibly representing a neonatal withdrawal syndrome (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy).

Propylene glycol toxicity from Tegretol suspension (25 mg propylene glycol per mL): hemolysis, hyperosmolarity with anion gap metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, CNS toxicity, multi-organ failure; neonates and children under 5 at highest risk (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Propylene Glycol Toxicity and OVERDOSAGE).
Status epilepticus with life-threatening hazard from abrupt discontinuation of any anticonvulsant drug in a responsive epileptic patient (Tegretol US PI, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Acute intermittent porphyria, variegate porphyria, porphyria cutanea tarda attacks reported in patients with a history of hepatic porphyria (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General and ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Hyponatremia, in many cases via SIADH, dose-related; can present with seizures, confusion, falls; elderly and diuretic-treated patients at greater risk; consider discontinuation if symptomatic (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - General).
food_interactions: Grapefruit juice: listed among CYP3A4 inhibitors that inhibit Tegretol metabolism and can thus increase plasma carbamazepine levels; close monitoring of carbamazepine levels is indicated and dosage adjustment may be required (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions, Agents That Increase Carbamazepine Levels; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5).

Alcohol: a possible additive sedative effect when taken in combination with Tegretol therapy - caution should be exercised (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients). UK SmPC: carbamazepine, like other psychoactive drugs, may reduce alcohol tolerance; it is therefore advisable for the patient to abstain from alcohol (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.5 - Combinations that require specific consideration). Combined poisoning: alcohol taken at the same time may aggravate or modify the signs and symptoms of acute Tegretol poisoning (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Combined Poisoning).

Food has no significant influence on the rate and extent of absorption of Tegretol, regardless of dosage form; medication should be taken with meals per US labeling (US PI, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 5.2 - Absorption).

Tegretol suspension should not be administered simultaneously with other liquid medicinal agents or diluents - precipitate formation reported with chlorpromazine solution and liquid thioridazine (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Drug Interactions).
Tegretol may be taken during, after or between meals, with a little liquid, e.g. a glass of water (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.2).
fields.pregnancy_category: The current FDA Tegretol Prescribing Information is in Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLR) format and does not assign a letter pregnancy category. It states: 'Carbamazepine can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.' Epidemiological data suggest that there may be an association between the use of carbamazepine during pregnancy and congenital malformations, including spina bifida; reports also associate carbamazepine with developmental disorders and congenital anomalies (craniofacial defects, cardiovascular malformations, and anomalies involving various body systems); developmental delays based on neurobehavioral assessments have been reported. The UK SmPC likewise assigns no letter category and states carbamazepine should not be used during pregnancy unless the benefit is judged to outweigh the risks, that epidemiological data show children born to mothers with epilepsy treated with carbamazepine in the first trimester are at increased risk of major congenital malformations (a meta-analysis reported 4.93% of children of epileptic women exposed to carbamazepine monotherapy in the first trimester suffer from congenital malformations, 95% CI 3.84-6.16, vs a background population rate of around 2-3%), and that women of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception. (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy; Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, sections 4.4 and 4.6)
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Carbamazepine can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Epidemiological data suggest an association between use of carbamazepine during pregnancy and congenital malformations, including spina bifida; there have also been reports associating carbamazepine with developmental disorders and congenital anomalies (e.g., craniofacial defects, cardiovascular malformations, anomalies involving various body systems); developmental delays based on neurobehavioral assessments have been reported. When treating or counseling women of childbearing potential, weigh the benefits of therapy against the risks; if this drug is used during pregnancy, or the patient becomes pregnant while taking it, the patient should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy). Retrospective case reviews suggest higher prevalence of teratogenic effects with anticonvulsant combination therapy than monotherapy; if therapy is to be continued, monotherapy may be preferable for pregnant women (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy). In humans, transplacental passage of carbamazepine is rapid (30 to 60 minutes), and the drug is accumulated in fetal tissues, with higher levels in liver and kidney than in brain and lung (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy). In rat teratology studies, 2 of 135 offspring showed kinked ribs at 250 mg/kg and 4 of 119 offspring at 650 mg/kg showed other anomalies (cleft palate, 1; talipes, 1; anophthalmos, 2); nursing offspring demonstrated a lack of weight gain and unkempt appearance at a maternal dosage of 200 mg/kg (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy). A few cases of neonatal seizures and/or respiratory depression associated with maternal Tegretol and other concomitant anticonvulsant use have been reported; a few cases of neonatal vomiting, diarrhea, and/or decreased feeding have also been reported, which may represent a neonatal withdrawal syndrome (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy and PRECAUTIONS - Labor and Delivery). Women with epilepsy who become pregnant should not abruptly discontinue antiepileptic drugs, including Tegretol, due to the risk of status epilepticus or severe seizures, which may be life-threatening; untreated or poorly controlled convulsive seizures carry the greatest risk of maternal or fetal injury; epilepsy (with or without AED exposure) is associated with preeclampsia, preterm labor, antepartum and postpartum hemorrhage, placental abruption, poor fetal growth, prematurity, fetal death, and maternal mortality (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy, Clinical Considerations). To provide information regarding effects of in utero exposure, pregnant patients taking Tegretol are advised to enroll in the North American Antiepileptic Drug (NAAED) Pregnancy Registry by calling the toll-free number 1-888-233-2334 (must be done by patients themselves); information also at http://www.aedpregnancyregistry.org/ (Tegretol US PI, WARNINGS - Usage in Pregnancy). UK SmPC: carbamazepine crosses the placenta; most common major congenital malformations reported include neural tube defects (spina bifida), craniofacial defects (cleft lip/palate), cardiovascular malformations, genitourinary tract defects (hypospadias), skeletal malformations; a meta-analysis showed 4.93% of children of epileptic women exposed to carbamazepine monotherapy in the first trimester suffer from congenital malformations (95% CI 3.84-6.16) vs ~2-3% background; risk may be dose-dependent (doses <400 mg/day associated with lower malformation rates); if no alternative is suitable and treatment continues, use monotherapy and the lowest effective dose, maintain plasma levels in the lower side of the therapeutic range (4-12 micrograms/mL), monitor plasma levels; specialized antenatal surveillance recommended; evidence suggests the risk of malformation may be dose-dependent; small-for-gestational-age births and neurodevelopmental disorders (developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, ADHD) have been reported, though studies on neurodevelopmental risk are contradictory and a risk cannot be excluded; carbamazepine may decrease serum folate - folic acid supplementation is recommended before and during pregnancy; in order to prevent bleeding disorders in the offspring, vitamin K1 has been recommended for the mother during the last weeks of pregnancy as well as to the neonate; if planning pregnancy, all efforts should be made to switch to appropriate alternative treatment prior to conception and before contraception is discontinued; if pregnancy occurs while on carbamazepine, refer to a specialist to reassess treatment and consider alternatives (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.6). Last two weeks of pregnancy vitamin K for mother and neonate - per UK SmPC only.
fields.lactation_guidance: US label: Tegretol and its epoxide metabolite are transferred to breast milk. The ratio of the concentration in breast milk to that in maternal plasma is about 0.4 for Tegretol and about 0.5 for the epoxide. The estimated doses given to the newborn during breastfeeding are in the range of 2 to 5 mg daily for Tegretol and 1 to 2 mg daily for the epoxide. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants from carbamazepine, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother (Tegretol US PI, PRECAUTIONS - Nursing Mothers). UK SmPC: carbamazepine passes into breast milk (about 25-60% of plasma concentrations). The benefits of breast-feeding should be weighed against the remote possibility of adverse effects occurring in the infant. Mothers taking Tegretol may breast-feed their infants, provided the infant is observed for possible adverse reactions (e.g., excessive somnolence, allergic skin reaction). There have been reports of cholestatic hepatitis in neonates exposed to carbamazepine during antenatal and/or breast feeding; breast-fed infants of mothers treated with carbamazepine should be carefully observed for adverse hepatobiliary effects (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.6 - Breastfeeding).
fields.overdose: Acute toxicity - lowest known lethal dose: adults, 3.2 g (a 24-year-old woman died of cardiac arrest and a 24-year-old man died of pneumonia and hypoxic encephalopathy); children, 4 g (a 14-year-old girl died of cardiac arrest), 1.6 g (a 3-year-old girl died of aspiration pneumonia). Oral LD50 in animals (mg/kg): mice, 1100 to 3750; rats, 3850 to 4025; rabbits, 1500 to 2680; guinea pigs, 920 (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Acute Toxicity). Signs and symptoms: the first signs and symptoms appear after 1 to 3 hours; neuromuscular disturbances are the most prominent; cardiovascular disorders are generally milder, and severe cardiac complications occur only when very high doses (greater than 60 g) have been ingested. Respiration: irregular breathing, respiratory depression. Cardiovascular: tachycardia, hypotension or hypertension, shock, conduction disorders. Nervous system and muscles: impairment of consciousness ranging in severity to deep coma; convulsions, especially in small children; motor restlessness, muscular twitching, tremor, athetoid movements, opisthotonos, ataxia, drowsiness, dizziness, mydriasis, nystagmus, adiadochokinesia, ballism, psychomotor disturbances, dysmetria; initial hyperreflexia, followed by hyporeflexia. GI tract: nausea, vomiting. Kidneys and bladder: anuria or oliguria, urinary retention. Laboratory findings: isolated instances have included leukocytosis, reduced leukocyte count, glycosuria, and acetonuria; EEG may show dysrhythmias (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Signs and Symptoms). Combined poisoning: when alcohol, tricyclic antidepressants, barbiturates, or hydantoins are taken at the same time, the signs and symptoms of acute poisoning with Tegretol may be aggravated or modified (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Combined Poisoning). Propylene glycol toxicity: in cases of suspected overdose with Tegretol suspension, which contains 25 mg of propylene glycol per mL, monitor for signs of propylene glycol toxicity, including hemolysis, hyperosmolarity with anion gap metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, CNS toxicity, and multi-organ failure (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Propylene Glycol Toxicity). Treatment: the prognosis in severe poisoning is critically dependent upon prompt elimination of the drug, which may be achieved by inducing vomiting, irrigating the stomach, and by taking appropriate steps to diminish absorption; there is no specific antidote. Elimination of the drug: induction of vomiting; gastric lavage - even when more than 4 hours have elapsed following ingestion, the stomach should be repeatedly irrigated, especially if the patient has also consumed alcohol. Measures to reduce absorption: activated charcoal, laxatives. Measures to accelerate elimination: forced diuresis. Dialysis is indicated only in severe poisoning associated with renal failure. Replacement transfusion is indicated in severe poisoning in small children. Respiratory depression: keep the airways free; resort, if necessary, to endotracheal intubation, artificial respiration, and administration of oxygen. Hypotension, shock: keep the patient's legs raised and administer a plasma expander; if blood pressure fails to rise despite measures to increase plasma volume, use of vasoactive substances should be considered. Convulsions: diazepam or barbiturates - warning: diazepam or barbiturates may aggravate respiratory depression (especially in children), hypotension, and coma; however, barbiturates should not be used if drugs that inhibit monoamine oxidase have also been taken by the patient either in overdosage or in recent therapy (within 1 week). Surveillance: respiration, cardiac function (ECG monitoring), blood pressure, body temperature, pupillary reflexes, and kidney and bladder function should be monitored for several days (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Treatment). Treatment of blood count abnormalities: if evidence of significant bone marrow depression develops - (1) stop the drug, (2) perform daily CBC, platelet, and reticulocyte counts, (3) do a bone marrow aspiration and trephine biopsy immediately and repeat with sufficient frequency to monitor recovery. Special periodic studies may be helpful: (1) white cell and platelet antibodies, (2) 59Fe-ferrokinetic studies, (3) peripheral blood cell typing, (4) cytogenetic studies on marrow and peripheral blood, (5) bone marrow culture studies for colony-forming units, (6) hemoglobin electrophoresis for A2 and F hemoglobin, (7) serum folic acid and B12 levels. A fully developed aplastic anemia will require appropriate, intensive monitoring and therapy, for which specialized consultation should be sought (Tegretol US PI, OVERDOSAGE - Treatment of Blood Count Abnormalities). UK SmPC adds: management initially guided by the patient's clinical condition, admission to hospital, measurement of the plasma level to confirm carbamazepine poisoning and ascertain overdose size; evacuation of the stomach, gastric lavage, activated charcoal (delay may result in delayed absorption and relapse during recovery); supportive care in an intensive care unit with cardiac monitoring and careful correction of electrolyte imbalance; charcoal haemoperfusion has been recommended; hemodialysis is the effective treatment modality in carbamazepine overdose; relapse and aggravation of symptomatology on the 2nd and 3rd day after overdose, due to delayed absorption, should be anticipated; CNS depression, convulsions, rhabdomyolysis, hyponatraemia, water intoxication due to ADH-like effect (Tegretol 100mg Tablets UK SmPC, section 4.9).
fields.pharmacokinetics: Absorption/bioavailability: in clinical studies, Tegretol suspension, conventional tablets, and XR tablets delivered equivalent amounts of drug to the systemic circulation; the suspension was absorbed somewhat faster, and the XR tablet slightly slower, than the conventional tablet; the bioavailability of the XR tablet was 89% compared to suspension. Following a twice a day dosage regimen, the suspension provides higher peak levels and lower trough levels than the conventional tablet; following a three times a day regimen, suspension affords steady-state plasma levels comparable to tablets given twice a day at the same total daily dose; following a twice a day regimen, Tegretol-XR affords steady-state plasma levels comparable to conventional tablets given four times a day at the same total daily dose. Tegretol in blood is 76% bound to plasma proteins; plasma levels are variable and may range from 0.5 to 25 mcg/mL with no apparent relationship to daily intake; usual adult therapeutic levels are between 4 and 12 mcg/mL. Following chronic oral administration of suspension, plasma levels peak at approximately 1.5 hours compared to 4 to 5 hours after conventional tablets, and 3 to 12 hours after Tegretol-XR tablets. The CSF/serum ratio is 0.22, similar to the 24% unbound Tegretol in serum. Because Tegretol induces its own metabolism, the half-life is variable; autoinduction is completed after 3 to 5 weeks of a fixed dosing regimen; initial half-life values range from 25 to 65 hours, decreasing to 12 to 17 hours on repeated doses. Tegretol is metabolized in the liver; cytochrome P450 3A4 was identified as the major isoform responsible for formation of carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide; human microsomal epoxide hydrolase is responsible for the 10,11-transdiol derivative. After oral administration of 14C-carbamazepine, 72% of radioactivity was found in the urine and 28% in the feces; urinary radioactivity was composed largely of hydroxylated and conjugated metabolites, with only 3% of unchanged Tegretol (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Pharmacokinetics). Children: pharmacokinetic parameters are similar in children and adults; poor correlation between plasma concentrations and dose in children; carbamazepine is more rapidly metabolized to the epoxide in younger age groups; in children below 15, there is an inverse relationship between CBZ-E/CBZ ratio and increasing age (0.44 in children below 1 year to 0.18 in children 10-15 years) (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Pharmacokinetics). Race and gender effects on carbamazepine pharmacokinetics have not been systematically evaluated (Tegretol US PI, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY - Pharmacokinetics).
